To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the financial crisis had an enormous impact on the EU’s economic governance and that this development is not only a struggle between hard and ‘soft’ law but also a struggle for the EU’s competence to interfere in national economic policy.
The EU has broadened its competences in the area of economic governance.
the financial crisis has triggered an expansion of EU competences and the EU’s role as global actor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can the EU’s economic governance be characterised as a form of global law?
the question of how the EU’s economic governance has changed in the wake of the financial and sovereign debt crisis.
the question how the EU has reacted to the global financial crisis and what this implies for the role of hard and soft law in the EU.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EU’s crisis response has been a success in the short run.
the financial crisis has led to a significant shift towards hard law and a significant expansion of EU competences.
the financial crisis has not changed the role of law in the EU, but has rather reinforced it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crisis has triggered the EU to act in a more integrated manner and has increased the EU’s competences, but at the same time has also triggered the Member States to act more in a national way.
we are not only witnessing a change of the role of law in the EU, but also in the global context.
we have shown how the EU is using its competences and the legal framework to deal with the crisis, but also how the EU’s competences are being extended to address the crisis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EU is not only a global actor but also a global law maker.
the EU’s crisis response has been characterised by an expansion of EU competences and a shift from soft to hard law.
the EU’s economic policy coordination is a multi-faceted phenomenon that is not limited to the traditional hard law of the EU Treaties.
